hypothesis: Reversible backtracking over indexed compatible candidate row pools can overcome the four-row dead-end of irreversible random greedy selection and assemble seven disjoint rulers at scope 111.
rationale: The random greedy family sampled many rows but committed irreversibly; retaining thousands of compatible row masks and revisiting earlier choices directly tests whether the bottleneck is search policy rather than absence of compatible rows.
expected_information_gain: Measures pool sizes, search depth, backtracking nodes, and whether a complete seven-row exact witness exists in the sampled multi-row neighborhood.
method: Keep rows 2,3,5 of the published witness fixed. For variable rows 0,1,4,6, sample unique internally Golomb rows within radius 25 of each published row or uniformly at scope <=111, filter against the fixed difference mask, then DFS over disjoint bitmasks with a 500000-node cap.
metric: candidate-pool size, deepest compatible assignment, and independent DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A seven-row assignment accepted by the independent validator is exactly the scope<=111 true target; pool depth and node counts are diagnostic search metrics only.
kill_condition: Stop after three 30-second seeded pool/backtracking runs or immediately on an independently validated target witness.
interpretation: Pre-registered reversible exact-cover-style search; no candidate claim is made until independent validation.
recommended_next_action: If successful, independently reproduce and generalize; if unsuccessful, use pool-depth evidence to choose between broader candidate generation and algebraic/SAT modeling.
